role: Vikram - Payment & financial integrity (RC 115f698, clean checkout at C:/Users/Sage world/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/rc-115f698)
summary: Money-in (wallet top-up via Razorpay order + HMAC webhook + hourly reconciliation) is the strongest path: signature fail-closed with boot-time placeholder guard, row-locked idempotent credit, amount/currency cross-check, ledger double-entry with pessimistic wallet locks. Money-out and secondary flows are not go-live safe. (1) Creator withdrawal is deterministically broken: the FE sends a 36-char UUID Idempotency-Key, WalletService namespaces it to an 80-char key and writes it (+':D'/':C') into VARCHAR(64) wallet_transactions.idempotency_key and payouts.idempotency_key; MySQL 8 strict mode rejects it at commit. (2) Worse, that whole withdrawal runs inside one @Transactional that calls RazorpayX BEFORE commit while holding PESSIMISTIC_WRITE locks on the creator wallet AND the platform clearing wallet, with no HTTP request timeout, and the idempotency row is marked COMPLETED in REQUIRES_NEW before the ambient commit - any commit failure after a successful gateway call leaves money sent with no debit, no payout row and a permanently wedged key. (3) Escrow: nothing server-side stops a milestone being funded twice (or re-funded after RELEASED/REFUNDED), and POST /wallet/escrow/refund lets a brand OWNER/ADMIN claw back a FUNDED milestone hold at any time short of a dispute freeze. (4) Affiliate commission settlement cannot work: Java enums AFFILIATE_COMMISSION/AFFILIATE_EARNING are absent from the DB ENUM columns, the credit targets a wallet owned by creator_profiles.id instead of users.id, and the commission is debited from the clearing wallet with no brand-side funding. (5) Payout reconciliation ignores RazorpayX 'failed' status/payout.failed and treats any gateway exception (incl. timeout) as a definitive failure and re-credits. 162 existing money-path tests pass (13 classes, exit 0) but they are Mockito-based and structurally cannot see the column-length, DB-enum, owner-id or transaction-ordering defects.

questions.question: Can a forged or replayed Razorpay webhook credit a wallet?
questions.why_it_matters: The webhook is the only path by which money enters a wallet.
questions.answer: Not with correct config. HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body with constant-time compare; blank secret fails closed; SecretsStartupValidator aborts non-dev boot if the webhook secret is blank or the committed placeholder. Replay of a genuine delivery is a no-op: confirmCredited row-locks the top-up and returns early when CREDITED, and the ledger key 'topup:<id>' is unique.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Prod env value of RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET not inspected (secret). No replay-window/timestamp check, but idempotency makes replay harmless for credits.

questions.question: Can a client tamper with the amount credited or debited?
questions.why_it_matters: Amount tampering is the classic payment-integrity hole.
questions.answer: Top-up amount is client-chosen by design but the webhook-reported captured amount/currency must exactly equal the persisted order amount before credit. Escrow fund amount is re-derived server-side from milestone/campaign (no amount field in the request). Withdrawal amount is client-supplied but bounded by locked balance and min/max. Withdrawal DTO has no @Digits, so 3-decimal amounts reach the ledger (see finding VIK-P3-01).
questions.evidence: WalletTopUpService.java:230-266; EscrowController.java:81-83 (deriveFundAmount); EscrowService.java:344-373; MoneyDtos.java:82 (CreatorWithdrawRequest has only @NotNull @DecimalMin), :103 (top-up has @Digits).

questions.question: Does creator withdrawal actually work end to end against MySQL?
questions.why_it_matters: It is the only money-out path a creator can trigger.
questions.answer: No. creator-wallet.tsx sends crypto.randomUUID() (36 chars); WalletService builds 'creator-withdraw:'+userId+':'+key = 80 chars, ledger appends ':D' = 82, and both wallet_transactions.idempotency_key and payouts.idempotency_key are VARCHAR(64). MySQL 8 (STRICT_TRANS_TABLES default, corroborated by migration V20260907120000 comment) rejects it. Any client key longer than 18 chars fails.
questions.evidence: src/pages/creator-wallet.tsx:593; src/lib/api.ts:4077-4082; WalletService.java:304,385-395,401-412; V8__wallet_transactions.sql:15; V48__payouts.sql:13; WalletTransaction.java:61; Payout.java:56; computed lengths: scoped=80, ledger leg=82, max fitting client key=18.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Not executed against a live MySQL in this audit (no safe DB available without authenticating). WalletServiceTest is Mockito-only so it cannot catch it.

questions.question: Is any external gateway call made before the DB transaction that records it commits?
questions.why_it_matters: Gateway-before-commit ordering is how money leaves without a ledger record.
questions.answer: Yes, in creator withdrawal: requestCreatorWithdrawal is @Transactional (public, proxied) and calls RazorpayX initiatePayout inside it before commit; the idempotency row is marked COMPLETED in a REQUIRES_NEW transaction before the ambient commit. PayoutService (milestone payout) deliberately avoids this by having no ambient transaction and a PENDING row + orphan sweep; withdrawal has neither.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Whether RazorpayX rejects an 80-char reference_id (its documented max is 40 chars, from memory, not verified here) decides whether today's deterministic commit failure is preceded by a real transfer.

questions.question: Can the same milestone be funded (debited) twice?
questions.why_it_matters: Double-debit of the brand and double-pay of the creator.
questions.answer: Yes, server-side. initiateFund dedupes only on the client Idempotency-Key; nothing checks the milestone's status or escrowHoldId, and PaymentMilestone.markFunded unconditionally overwrites escrowHoldId and status (even from RELEASED/REFUNDED). Release keys are per-hold ('release:<holdId>'), so a second hold can be released again. Only the FE hides the button.
questions.evidence: EscrowService.java:240-259,261-274,291-333,495-503; PaymentMilestone.java:141-145; deal-payments-tab.tsx:194 (FE-only canFund guard); useEscrowFund.ts:203-205 (fresh key per new submission).
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Not runtime-reproduced; no test covers a second fund on the same milestone.

questions.question: Can a brand take escrowed money back after the creator has started work, outside a dispute?
questions.why_it_matters: Creator protection is the product's core promise; the published policy says no on-demand refund.
questions.answer: Yes via API. POST /wallet/escrow/refund is live for OWNER/ADMIN and refundInternal only blocks on a dispute freeze; it does not check collaboration status, deliverable submission/approval, or release condition. The controller javadoc admits it has no FE caller and contradicts the policy.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Whether ops intends this as a back-office primitive; it is not role-restricted to admins.

questions.question: Are ledger idempotency keys within column length on every path?
questions.why_it_matters: Overflow either fails the money movement or (non-strict) truncates keys and collapses the :D/:C legs.
questions.answer: Server-derived keys fit (topup: 34, escrow-fund: 40, dispute-split-release: 50, release-fee: 40, brand-fee-publish: 46, payout-debit: 41, payout retry keys hashed to <=56, affiliate 'prefix+redemptionId'). Only the creator-withdraw key overflows. Admin manual payout passes the raw client header straight into the ledger (fits for a UUID but is the unscoped-key pattern the codebase itself calls CRITICAL elsewhere).
questions.evidence: WalletTopUpService.java:211; EscrowService.java:480,683,913,990,1253,1291,1354,1374; PlatformFeeService.java:98; BrandCampaignFeeService.java:200; PayoutService.java:488; PayoutReconciliationService.java:380-428; admin/AdminFinanceService.java:216-226.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Affiliate DERIVED_KEY_PREFIX length not printed; redemption ids are 26-char ULIDs.

questions.question: Is there a reconciliation path for money captured at Razorpay but never credited?
questions.why_it_matters: A lost webhook otherwise strands customer money silently.
questions.answer: Yes for top-ups: WalletTopUpReconciliationJob (hourly, ShedLock) fetches order state for PENDING top-ups aged 20 min - 7 days and credits through the same confirmCredited path. Nothing reconciles top-ups older than 7 days, and no refund/chargeback events are handled.
questions.evidence: job/WalletTopUpReconciliationJob.java (GRACE 20m, GIVE_UP 7d, cron 0 35 * * * *); RazorpayClient.java:165-193; WalletTopUpReconciliationJobTest 8/8 pass; RazorpayWebhookController.java:97-153 (no refund.* / payment.dispute.* cases).
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Job not observed running in prod.

questions.question: Are RazorpayX payout terminal states fully handled?
questions.why_it_matters: An unhandled failure status strands the creator's debited money.
questions.answer: Partially. Webhook routes processed/reversed/rejected/cancelled only; FAILURE_STATUSES excludes 'failed', so a payout.failed event (if RazorpayX sends one) is ACKed by the default branch and the queue-time debit is never re-credited. attemptGatewayPayout treats any exception (including a read timeout on a payout that actually succeeded) as a definitive failure and re-credits.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Exact RazorpayX status/event list taken from recall of its API, not verified in this audit.

questions.question: Does affiliate commission ever reach a creator?
questions.why_it_matters: Creators are promised commission on coupon sales.
questions.answer: No. Three independent blockers: DB ENUMs lack AFFILIATE_COMMISSION/AFFILIATE_EARNING (insert fails under strict mode); the credit goes to a wallet keyed on creator_profiles.id rather than users.id (invisible to the creator); and the debit comes from the clearing wallet with no brand charge.
questions.evidence: WalletTransactionType.java (AFFILIATE_COMMISSION), TxnReferenceType.java (AFFILIATE_EARNING); V8__wallet_transactions.sql:5-6,11 (ENUMs without them; no later ALTER); job/AffiliateSettlementWriter.java:129-142; V28__affiliate_earnings_settlement.sql:53 (creator_id FK creator_profiles); AuthService.java:427-428 (profileId distinct ULID); WalletService.java:693-698.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Affiliate tests are Mockito-only, so none of this has been executed against a schema.

questions.question: Is the brand publish fee charged exactly once and correctly?
questions.why_it_matters: Double charge or skipped charge on every campaign.
questions.answer: Exactly once per campaign via ledger key 'brand-fee-publish:<campaignId>' on both the PATCH and Meera paths. But a PAUSED campaign whose budget was edited can never be re-activated: the replay has a different amount, and assertReplayMatches throws LEDGER_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_COLLISION (409).
questions.evidence: BrandCampaignFeeService.java:171-238; CampaignService.java:273-274,368-377; ConfirmLaunchExecutor.java:338-340; CampaignValidator.java ensureEditable(current,statusOnlyPatch) allows edits when not ACTIVE; WalletLedgerService.java:91-95,225-246.

questions.question: Are subscription webhooks safe against out-of-order and cross-subscription events?
questions.why_it_matters: Wrong status downgrades a paying customer or keeps a cancelled one active.
questions.answer: Per-delivery dedupe plus a created_at staleness check exist. However, an event for an OLD Razorpay subscription id falls back to findByWorkspaceId and is applied to the workspace's current row, relinking it to the dead subscription (e.g. a late subscription.cancelled for sub_A after the brand re-subscribed as sub_B).
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Whether initiateCheckout permits a new subscription while an old one is pending cancel-at-cycle-end was not traced.

questions.question: Is BigDecimal scale/rounding consistent across fee, GST and paise conversion?
questions.why_it_matters: Paisa drift breaks reconciliation and invoices.
questions.answer: Mostly. Fees use HALF_UP at 2dp with net = gross - fee (no drift); GST CGST/SGST split absorbs the residual; paise conversion uses longValueExact (throws on >2dp instead of rounding silently). Gaps: withdrawal amount has no @Digits; GST defaults to IGST whenever the customer GSTIN is blank, which is wrong for intra-state unregistered (B2C) customers.
questions.evidence: PlatformFeeService.java:50-57; BrandCampaignFeeService.java:182-185; GstSplitUtil.java:24-41; RazorpayXClient.java:126; RazorpayClient.java:108; MoneyDtos.java:82.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Invoice-number sequencing and PDF paths not traced line by line.

questions.question: Is TDS (194-O / 194-R) withheld on creator earnings or payouts?
questions.why_it_matters: Statutory liability for a marketplace paying individuals.
questions.answer: No automated TDS. The only TDS artefact is payouts.tds_amount, recorded by an admin on a manual payout; the ledger debits the full amount and books no TDS liability. Memory notes TDS was deliberately ruled out pending a spec and CA gate, so this is a known, parked compliance gap, not a regression.
questions.evidence: V71__payouts_manual_rail.sql (tds_amount column); admin/AdminFinanceService.java:178-226 (ledger posts full amount; TDS only stored on Payout).
questions.remaining_uncertainty: The legal ruling itself was not opened (doc, not evidence).

findings.title: Creator withdrawal calls RazorpayX inside an uncommitted DB transaction while holding wallet + clearing-wallet row locks, and marks idempotency COMPLETED before commit
findings.evidence: WalletService.requestCreatorWithdrawal is public @Transactional (WalletService.java:249-250) and takes PESSIMISTIC_WRITE on the creator wallet (:263-265, WalletRepository.java:17-19). Inside it, executeOnce runs doProcessWithdrawal (its own @Transactional at :381 is inert: protected + self-invoked via lambda at :311), which calls ledgerService.post (joins the ambient tx, locks the platform clearing wallet row FOR UPDATE, WalletLedgerService.java:102-103), then razorpayXClient.initiatePayout (:398-399, real HTTP), then payoutRepository.save (:401-412). IdempotencyService.executeOnce marks the key COMPLETED in REQUIRES_NEW right after action.get() returns (IdempotencyService.java:157-159; IdempotencyReservationOps.java:144-148), i.e. BEFORE the ambient commit. RazorpayXClient builds the request with no .timeout() (RazorpayXClient.java:138-145; only connectTimeout at :86). Contrast PayoutService, which intentionally has no ambient transaction and persists a PENDING row plus an orphan sweep (PayoutService.java:417-433,460-473).
findings.impact: Any commit-time failure after RazorpayX accepts the payout (such as the deterministic key-length failure in VIK-P1-01, a deadlock, or a connection drop) rolls back the ledger debit and the payout row while the bank transfer stands. There is then no payouts row for the webhook to reconcile against ('No Payout row found... acknowledged', PayoutReconciliationService.java:123-131). The key is COMPLETED, so a retry returns 409 forever, and the FE mints a fresh key on the next dialog, so the same balance can be withdrawn again. Separately, the platform clearing-wallet row lock is held for the whole unbounded RazorpayX HTTP call, which stalls every top-up credit, escrow fund/release, fee and payout platform-wide.
findings.recommended_fix: Restructure withdrawal like PayoutService: remove @Transactional from requestCreatorWithdrawal; commit a PENDING Payout row plus the ledger debit in one short transaction (through a separate bean so it is really transactional); call RazorpayX outside any transaction; then record the gateway result in a second transaction. Mark the idempotency row COMPLETED only after that commit. Extend PayoutOrphanedDebitSweepJob to cover withdrawal rows (milestoneId null). Add HttpRequest.timeout() to every RazorpayX/Razorpay call.
findings.verification_required: Integration test on MySQL (Testcontainers) that forces a commit failure after a stubbed successful initiatePayout and asserts a durable PENDING/QUEUED payouts row and debit survive. Also a lock-hold test showing no clearing-wallet lock is held during the gateway call.
affected_features: All ledger movements touching the clearing wallet (availability)
findings.reproduction: Static: follow the call chain above. Runtime repro requires MySQL + a RazorpayX sandbox that accepts the payout; not performed.

findings.title: Withdrawal idempotency key (80 chars from a UUID header) overflows VARCHAR(64) in wallet_transactions and payouts, so every FE withdrawal fails at commit
findings.evidence: FE: creator-wallet.tsx:593 uses safeRandomUUID() (crypto.randomUUID, 36 chars; fallback 'idem-...' 25 chars). BE: WalletService.java:304 scopedKey = 'creator-withdraw:' + userId(26) + ':' + key = 80 chars; passed as the ledger key (:394), where WalletLedgerService.java:159,178 appends ':D'/':C' (82 chars), and as Payout.idempotencyKey (:411). Columns: V8__wallet_transactions.sql:15 VARCHAR(64); V48__payouts.sql:13 VARCHAR(64); entity length=64 (WalletTransaction.java:61, Payout.java:56). No length validation in WalletController.java:116-125. Any client key over 18 chars overflows. MySQL 8.0 images (deploy/*/docker-compose*.yml) default to STRICT_TRANS_TABLES (acknowledged live in V20260907120000 comment line 40). WalletServiceTest is Mockito-only (@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class), :60) with a short constant key, so the 27 passing tests cannot see it. Mock/dev mode also overflows payouts.razorpay_payout_id VARCHAR(64) with 'payout_stub_'+80 chars (RazorpayXClient.java:123).
findings.impact: Creator withdrawal, the only creator-initiated money-out, fails 100% of the time from the shipped FE (500 / Data too long). The idempotency row is left COMPLETED (see VIK-P0-01), so retrying with the same key returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_PROGRESS permanently. Combined with VIK-P0-01, if RazorpayX accepts the request the money leaves anyway. This is still open from the 2026-09-17 audit.
findings.recommended_fix: Derive a fixed-width key: 'cw:' + sha256(userId + ':' + clientKey) truncated to 40 hex chars, which also fits RazorpayX's reference_id limit. Reject client keys over 64 chars at the controller. Add a MySQL-backed test that posts a UUID-keyed withdrawal.
findings.verification_required: Testcontainers MySQL test calling POST /wallet/withdraw with a UUID Idempotency-Key and asserting 200 plus one debit leg plus one payouts row.
findings.reproduction: Length arithmetic run in this audit: uuid_len=36 scopedKey_len=80 ledger_leg_len=82 > 64; max fitting client key = 18.

findings.title: No server-side guard against funding the same milestone twice, or re-funding a RELEASED/REFUNDED milestone
findings.evidence: EscrowService.initiateFund (EscrowService.java:212-335) dedupes only on the client Idempotency-Key (:261-274). assertContractActiveForMilestone (:388-434) checks signatures and cancellation but never milestone.status or milestone.escrowHoldId. applyFunding (:495-503) calls milestone.markFunded(hold.getId()), which unconditionally sets escrowHoldId and status=FUNDED (PaymentMilestone.java:141-145), even from RELEASED. Release uses per-hold keys 'release:'+holdId (:913), so the new hold is releasable again, and the ledger will debit the brand and credit the creator a second time. The only guard is FE-side (deal-payments-tab.tsx:194 canFund); useEscrowFund.ts:203-205 mints a new key per fresh submission.
findings.impact: Two tabs, a stale page, an API client or Meera replay under a new key debits the brand twice for one milestone; the first hold is orphaned FUNDED (milestone now points at hold 2). A RELEASED milestone can be flipped back to FUNDED and paid a second time. Brand money is double-committed and the creator can be double-paid.
findings.recommended_fix: In initiateFund, lock the milestone row (findByIdForUpdate) and reject unless status == PENDING and escrowHoldId == null (409 MILESTONE_ALREADY_FUNDED). Make PaymentMilestone.markFunded assert the PENDING precondition. Optionally add a unique index on escrow_holds(milestone_id) filtered to live statuses (via a generated column).
findings.verification_required: Test: fund milestone M with key k1, then with key k2; expect 409 and exactly one ESCROW_HOLD debit. Test: fund after RELEASED; expect 409.

findings.title: Brand can refund a FUNDED milestone escrow hold on demand (no deliverable/collaboration gate), bypassing dispute resolution
findings.evidence: EscrowController.java:152-166 exposes POST /wallet/escrow/refund to any brand principal, and EscrowService.refund (:959-970) enforces OWNER/ADMIN only. refundInternal (:972-1015) checks workspace, REFUNDED no-op, dispute freeze (:981-986) and FUNDED state. It does not check collaboration status, submitted/approved deliverables, or release_condition, and it applies to milestone-backed holds (marks milestone REFUNDED, :1004-1012). The controller javadoc (:138-151) states the published refund policy allows no on-demand refund and that the route has no FE caller.
findings.impact: After a creator has delivered (or even after brand approval, before auto-release fires), the brand can pull the full escrow back to its spendable wallet with one API call. The creator is unpaid and the only recourse is a dispute, which cannot freeze money that has already left escrow. This contradicts the platform's payment-protection promise.
findings.recommended_fix: Restrict /wallet/escrow/refund to holds with no milestone, or to collaborations in CANCELLED/never-started state with no submitted deliverables. Otherwise move it behind admin roles (AdminFinanceService with MFA). Milestone-backed refunds should go only through DisputeService.
findings.verification_required: Test: FUNDED milestone hold with a SUBMITTED deliverable, then brand refund; expect 409.

findings.title: Affiliate settlement writes WalletTransactionType.AFFILIATE_COMMISSION / TxnReferenceType.AFFILIATE_EARNING, which are not in the DB ENUMs
findings.evidence: WalletTransactionType.java adds AFFILIATE_COMMISSION; TxnReferenceType.java adds AFFILIATE_EARNING. wallet_transactions.type/reference_type are MySQL ENUMs without them (V8__wallet_transactions.sql:5-6,11), and no later migration alters wallet_transactions (grep across db/migration). WalletTransaction maps them @Enumerated(STRING) (WalletTransaction.java:30-51). AffiliateSettlementWriter.creditCreatorWallet posts them (job/AffiliateSettlementWriter.java:132-142). The only tests are Mockito (CreatorAffiliateEarningSettlementTest:59), and they pass.
findings.impact: Under strict mode the INSERT fails ('Data truncated for column type'), doSettleCreator rolls back, and every PENDING earning is retried and fails forever: affiliate commission is never credited. This is still open from the 2026-09-17 audit.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a migration: ALTER TABLE wallet_transactions MODIFY type ENUM(...,'AFFILIATE_COMMISSION'), MODIFY reference_type ENUM(...,'AFFILIATE_EARNING'). Add a schema-conformance test that compares every Java enum persisted as STRING against the DB ENUM definition.
findings.verification_required: Flyway-on-MySQL test that settles one earning and reads back the ledger rows.

findings.title: Affiliate commission credited to a wallet owned by creator_profiles.id, not the creator's users.id
findings.evidence: affiliate_earnings.creator_id is FK creator_profiles(id) (V28__affiliate_earnings_settlement.sql:53,74), copied from coupon_codes.creator_id, also FK creator_profiles (V24__coupon_codes.sql:29,47; AffiliateEarningsService.java doRecordEarning .creatorId(coupon.getCreatorId())). AffiliateSettlementWriter.java:130 calls walletService.requireOrCreateUserWallet(earning.getCreatorId()), which creates or looks up a wallet by ownerId=profileId (WalletService.java:693-698). Creator reads use principal.getUserId() (WalletService.getBalanceForUser/getSummaryForUser, :129-138,208-226), and the profile id is a distinct ULID (AuthService.java:427-428).
findings.impact: Once VIK-P1-04 is fixed, every commission lands in an orphan USER wallet the creator can never see or withdraw. The money is stranded and the creator dashboard shows nothing.
findings.recommended_fix: Resolve creatorProfileRepository.findById(earning.getCreatorId()).getUserId() before requireOrCreateUserWallet. Backfill or merge any orphan wallets keyed by profile ids.
findings.verification_required: Integration test: settle an earning, then GET /wallet/balance as that creator and see the commission.

findings.title: Affiliate commission is funded from the platform clearing wallet with no brand-side debit
findings.evidence: AffiliateSettlementWriter.java:131-142 posts clearing wallet (debit) to creator wallet (credit). AffiliateSettlementJob.java has no workspace/brand wallet reference (grep 'workspace|brand|post(' returns only javadoc). The clearing wallet is exempt from the non-negative check (WalletLedgerService.java:131-139), so the debit always succeeds and goes negative.
findings.impact: Commission is paid out of the pooled cash that backs brand deposits and escrow. The clearing account stops reconciling to the Razorpay/bank balance, and the platform silently absorbs every commission. Latent today only because VIK-P1-04/05 block settlement.
findings.recommended_fix: Debit the brand workspace wallet (or a dedicated brand-funded commission pool) at earning or settlement time, with an insufficient-balance policy, before crediting the creator.
findings.verification_required: After settlement, clearing wallet delta = 0 and brand wallet delta = -commission.

findings.title: Payout failure handling: RazorpayX 'failed' status is not a failure status, and any gateway exception is treated as a definitive failure and re-credited
findings.evidence: Webhook routes only payout.processed/reversed/rejected/cancelled (RazorpayWebhookController.java:109-110); other payout.* events fall to the no-op default (:148-152). FAILURE_STATUSES = reversed/rejected/cancelled (PayoutReconciliationService.java:63-64,95-99); 'failed' is absent. attemptGatewayPayout catches Exception, including a read hang/timeout, marks REVERSED and re-credits (:254-266). No request timeout on RazorpayX calls (RazorpayXClient.java:138-145), and retries use a new gateway key in retryFailedPayout (:422-424,453-454).
findings.impact: (a) A payout RazorpayX marks 'failed' leaves the creator's debit stranded with no re-credit. (b) A sweep/retry call that times out after RazorpayX actually accepted it is marked REVERSED and re-credited; the later payout.processed webhook carries the real pout_ id, which does not match the row's 'pending:<id>' placeholder, so it is ACKed without effect and the creator is paid twice.
findings.recommended_fix: Add 'failed' to FAILURE_STATUSES and route payout.failed (also payout.updated). On a gateway exception, distinguish a definitive 4xx from transport errors: for transport errors, fetch the payout by reference_id/idempotency before reversing, and never reverse on a timeout. Add HttpRequest.timeout().
findings.verification_required: Confirm the RazorpayX event/status list against current docs; unit test attemptGatewayPayout with an HttpTimeoutException and assert no re-credit.
findings.reproduction: Static; RazorpayX status names from recall of its API docs.

findings.title: Resuming a PAUSED campaign whose budget was edited fails with LEDGER_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_COLLISION (409)
findings.evidence: transitioningToActive = status != ACTIVE && newStatus == ACTIVE (CampaignService.java:273-274), so PAUSED->ACTIVE re-runs chargeOnPublish (:375-377). The fee key is 'brand-fee-publish:'+campaignId (BrandCampaignFeeService.java:200) with fee = budgetMax x bps (:182-185). CampaignValidator.ensureEditable(current, statusOnlyPatch) allows a budget edit while PAUSED. The ledger fast path replays the existing posting and assertReplayMatches rejects the amount mismatch (WalletLedgerService.java:91-95,225-246).
findings.impact: A brand that pauses, raises or lowers the budget, and resumes gets an opaque 409 and the campaign can never go live again. An unchanged budget is fine (replay, no double charge).
findings.recommended_fix: Charge the publish fee only on the first activation (persist feeChargedAt / feePostingId on Campaign) and handle a budget delta explicitly (top-up fee on increase, policy on decrease), or version the key per budget revision.
findings.verification_required: Test: publish at 10k, pause, patch budget to 20k, resume; expect a defined outcome, not 409.

findings.title: Subscription webhook for a stale Razorpay subscription id is applied to the workspace's current row (fallback by workspaceId) and relinks it
findings.evidence: SubscriptionService.applySubscriptionWebhookUpdate looks up findByRazorpaySubscriptionId(id).or(findByWorkspaceId(ws)) (SubscriptionService.java:717-721), applies targetStatus, and calls linkRazorpaySubscription(incomingId) (:770-774; Subscription.java:204-212). The staleness guard compares only created_at (:752-762), not subscription identity. subscription.cancelled/completed map to CANCELLED (RazorpayWebhookController.java:146-147).
findings.impact: A brand that cancelled sub_A at cycle end and re-subscribed as sub_B is downgraded to CANCELLED when Razorpay later finalizes sub_A. The row is relinked to the dead id, so sub_B's future events no longer match by id either. The Pro fee rate and entitlements are lost for a paying customer.
findings.recommended_fix: If the row's razorpaySubscriptionId is non-null and differs from the incoming id, apply only if the incoming event is an activation of a newer subscription; otherwise ignore and log.
findings.verification_required: Test the sequence: sub_A cancel-at-end, sub_B charged, sub_A cancelled; expect the row to stay ACTIVE on sub_B.
findings.reproduction: Static; checkout re-subscribe precondition not traced.

findings.title: No handling of Razorpay refund/chargeback events for credited top-ups
findings.evidence: RazorpayWebhookController.receive switch (:97-153) has no refund.*, payment.refunded or payment.dispute.* cases; the default ACKs silently. Nothing in WalletTopUpService reverses a CREDITED top-up.
findings.impact: A top-up refunded from the Razorpay dashboard, or lost in a chargeback, stays spendable in the brand wallet (it can fund escrow and be paid to creators), creating an unbacked balance.
findings.recommended_fix: Route refund.processed and payment.dispute.lost to a reversal posting (brand wallet to clearing) with a negative-balance/freeze policy; alert ops.
findings.verification_required: Webhook test with a refund.processed payload for a credited top-up.

findings.title: Campaign-level pool hold satisfies the activation gate but has no product path to release or refund it
findings.evidence: Activation requires any FUNDED hold for the campaign (CampaignService.java:704-714), and a pool hold (no milestone) qualifies. Pool holds have collaborationId null (EscrowService.java:312-319); releaseByHoldIdInternal throws ESCROW_HOLD_NOT_LINKED (:648-658). Refund exists only via an API route with no FE caller (EscrowController.java:138-151). Milestones must then be funded separately (initiateFund with milestoneId), a second debit for the same budget.
findings.impact: Brand budget is locked twice (pool + milestones). The pool money sits FUNDED with no in-product exit unless Meera's bindCollaboration path runs. This matches the 2026-09-17 'pool-hold double debit' item and is still present.
findings.recommended_fix: Either let milestone funding draw down from an existing pool hold, or stop counting pool holds for activation and require milestone funding only. Provide a brand-visible refund for unbound pool holds.
findings.verification_required: E2E: fund pool, activate, sign contract, fund milestone; compare wallet debits to budget.

findings.title: WalletLedgerService catch(DataIntegrityViolationException) around plain save() is dead code; concurrent duplicate postings surface as raw 500 at commit
findings.evidence: WalletLedgerService.java:182-201 wraps walletRepository.save / walletTransactionRepository.save in try/catch(DataIntegrityViolationException). WalletTransaction has an assigned ULID id and no @Version, so SimpleJpaRepository.save does merge(), with the INSERT deferred to flush/commit outside the catch. This is the known save-vs-saveAndFlush trap.
findings.impact: No double-credit (the unique constraint still rolls back the loser), but a concurrent duplicate returns 500 instead of a replay. For the Razorpay webhook that means a non-2xx and a retry, and every such case is logged as an unexpected error.
findings.recommended_fix: Use saveAndFlush for the two legs (inside the try), or remove the misleading catch.
findings.verification_required: Concurrency test with two threads posting the same key on MySQL.

findings.title: CreatorWithdrawRequest.amount has no @Digits(fraction=2)
findings.evidence: MoneyDtos.java:82 (@NotNull @DecimalMin only), whereas the top-up DTO has @Digits (:103). RazorpayXClient.java:126 longValueExact throws ArithmeticException for more than 2dp, and the ledger stores DECIMAL(14,2).
findings.impact: A 3-decimal amount yields a 500 in configured mode; in mock mode the in-memory balance and the persisted DECIMAL(14,2) diverge by a sub-paisa amount.

findings.title: Admin manual payout uses the raw client Idempotency-Key as the ledger key; replay 500s on payouts unique key
findings.evidence: admin/AdminFinanceService.java:216-226 passes idempotencyKey unscoped into ledgerService.post (the pattern WalletTopUpService.java:203-211 calls [SEC: Kabir OWASP CRITICAL]). A same-key replay hits the ledger fast-path replay and then payoutRepository.save with a duplicate payouts.idempotency_key, giving a unique violation at commit (500). Keys over 62 chars overflow.
findings.impact: Admin-only (SUPER_ADMIN + MFA). The effect is a confusing 500 on double-submit and possible key collision with an unrelated posting (guarded by assertReplayMatches).
findings.recommended_fix: Namespace and hash the key ('manual-payout:' + sha256(...)); check payoutRepository.findByIdempotencyKey first and return the prior result.

findings.title: GST split defaults to IGST whenever customer GSTIN is blank (intra-state B2C mis-taxed)
findings.evidence: GstSplitUtil.java:29-40: intraState only when both GSTIN state codes match; a blank customer GSTIN gives IGST.
findings.impact: For unregistered customers the place of supply is their address state. Same-state customers should get CGST+SGST, so invoices are mis-classified (compliance, not cash).
findings.recommended_fix: Use the billing-address state when no GSTIN is present; get CA confirmation.
findings.verification_required: CA review plus a unit test.

findings.title: Top-up reconciliation gives up after 7 days and records the order id (not payment id) as gatewayRef
findings.evidence: WalletTopUpReconciliationJob: GIVE_UP_AFTER = 7 days; the query uses a createdAt window, and confirmCredited is passed topUp.getRazorpayOrderId() as gatewayRef.
findings.impact: A captured payment whose webhook and first 7 days of sweeps all fail is never credited, with no alert. Ledger gateway_ref is inconsistent between webhook (pay_...) and sweep (order_...) credits.
findings.recommended_fix: After give-up, raise a durable ops alert or open an incident row; store the payment id from the order's payments fetch.
